fields.description:
Discovered while repairing binding-drift bug 8656-01fe-6f74-44c9 (unbound_jira REB-3510).

DEFECT: the inbound-create adopt path writes the Jira-side rebar-id:<local-id> label BEFORE the local CREATE event + binding are durably published to origin/tickets. When the pass's final tickets push is rejected (non-fast-forward) on an EPHEMERAL runner (GHA run 32602702883: 'final-push-rejected … 7 unpushed commits', runner destroyed), the local state is lost while the Jira label persists. Every automated healing path then stands down:
- binding_walk L10 guard skips adopt when the rebar-id label is present
- differ's bug-4354 suppression likewise stands down on the label
- BindingRecovery.recover_pending_bindings only walks state=='pending' store entries, which were lost with the runner

Result: a permanently stuck unbound_jira drift that only manual repair (or the fsck canary + human) can clear. This class will recur on any ephemeral-runner reconcile that loses its final push race.

## Chosen design (AC1): option (b) — recovery extension, mechanizing the manual repair

Codebase evaluation of the two AC1 options:

- (a) durable-publish-first ordering was evaluated and REJECTED as the load-bearing fix. The label write-back (`_inbound_create_writeback_jira`) runs per-mutation inside `_apply_batch`'s dispatch loop; deferring it until after the pass's final `commit_and_push_tickets_branch` would restructure the apply loop, widen the bug-4354 window (the label is the differ's within-pass and next-pass dedup signal), and STILL leave the mirror-image window (local published, label stamp lost). Notably, that mirror window is ALREADY healed idempotently today: the ticket-1577 dedup guard in `_apply_inbound_create` (binding present -> `dedup_skipped`) makes replay safe when local state survived. The one unhandled ordering is exactly its converse — label persisted, local state lost — so the symmetric completion of the existing idempotent-replay design is the recovery extension, not a reordering.
- (b) recovery extension is the load-bearing fix. This matches what mature OSS systems do for cross-system crash windows (transactional-outbox consumers, Debezium/Kafka Connect source connectors resuming idempotently from offsets, Temporal activity retries, Stripe idempotent replay): pair best-effort ordering with IDEMPOTENT RECOVERY keyed on a deterministic identity — here the deterministic inbound local id (`_jira_key_to_local_id`), which makes the replayed adopt converge on the same local id, binding, and (idempotent re-add) the same Jira label.

Implementation: the fix lands in `binding_walk.py`'s phase-1b unbound arm — the level-triggered walk that already re-considers every present-unbound key each pass and whose L10 guard comment already promises "binding recovery owns re-linking a marked-but-unstored key" (a promise nothing fulfills today). The L10 stand-down becomes conditional: when the unbound key's rebar-id marker set is exactly the DETERMINISTIC inbound id for that key (`jira-<key-lower>`), AND the binding store has no entry (pending or confirmed) for that id, AND a targeted local read (`local_reader`) finds no local ticket — i.e. the marked-but-unstored lost-adopt residue — the walk falls through to the ordinary classify->ADOPT machinery instead of standing down. The replayed adopt routes through the EXISTING `_apply_inbound_create` leaf unchanged (retired-skip gate, dedup guard, baseline seed, idempotent label write-back) and through the existing blast-radius breaker and census.

Safety scoping (why this cannot re-introduce L11 double-bind): a marker that does NOT equal the deterministic inbound id (a UUID from an outbound bind, a foreign `jira-dig-NNNN` ghost label, or multiple markers) keeps the unconditional stand-down — those are different drift classes owned by dd-5 conflict surfacing / fsck alert + human adjudication. A key whose marked id still has a store entry keeps the stand-down (pending-write-ahead recovery owns it). A key whose marked local ticket still exists keeps the stand-down (only the binding is missing — a store_integrity repair, not this class). A RETIRED key still routes to SKIP_RETIRED via the classifier and the leaf's gate #1.

`bridge_fsck` is deliberately untouched (AC3): its unbound_jira audit classifies present-unbound snapshot keys without consulting the label, so it keeps alerting on this class until the binding actually exists again — no suppression.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Recovery extension per option (b): `binding_walk.py`'s unbound arm detects a marked-but-unstored key (rebar-id label equal to the deterministic inbound local id; no binding-store entry for that id; no local ticket) and replays the adopt through the existing inbound-create leaf, instead of standing down on the L10 guard. `compute_binding_walk_mutations` complexity does not increase (guard swapped one-for-one into a helper).
- [ ] A RED-first regression test simulating the lost-final-push runner: runner 1 adopts (CREATE event + binding written, label stamped), the final push is rejected and ALL local state is discarded; runner 2 (fresh store, fresh tracker) sees the labeled snapshot — the walk emits the replay adopt and applying it re-materialises the local ticket + binding under the SAME deterministic local id with no duplicate label. Confirmed failing (walk stands down, adopted == []) before the fix.
- [ ] Existing L10/L11 protections preserved: foreign/ghost markers, multi-marker keys, keys whose marked id still has a store entry, and keys whose marked local ticket still exists all keep standing down; retired keys still skip. Existing tests `test_class_b_labeled_key_not_double_bound` and `test_class_b_empty_rebar_id_marker_is_adopted` unchanged and green.
- [ ] bridge fsck continues to alert unbound_jira on the class until healed — no suppression added anywhere (fsck code untouched; post-heal the key is bound so the alert clears by becoming true).

## Testing / Verification

- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_binding_walk.py tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_apply_inbound_adopt.py -q` — new marked-but-unstored replay cells (walk-level + end-to-end two-runner replay) plus all existing class-A/B/C cells green.
- RED evidence recorded on the ticket: the new walk-level test fails on pre-fix code with `adopted == []` (stand-down on the label).
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` (includes the complexity ratchet: new=0 increased=0) and `make typecheck` green.
- fsck behavior verified by reading `bridge_fsck.py`'s unbound_jira audit (label not consulted) — no code change there.

Evidence and full RCA on ticket 8656-01fe-6f74-44c9; repair precedent 16c1-0f0c.
